units: MiB except explicitly named seconds and counts
scope: Six isolated local services; selected 12 seeded plus 2 ingested documents; no remote inference or production histories. One-second cgroup samples and endpoint process PSS.

image_audit.historical_identity_limit: The four repeats record immutable identities of all six services. Only the initial baseline1 and candidate1 runs lack per-run immutable identity capture; their tags match retained build identities.

interpretation: All final endpoints have 17 web processes; intermediate post-metadata endpoints baseline2 and candidate1 include an extra Celery worker and are not directly comparable as idle PSS.
Use final application/web PSS and anonymous-memory differences for attribution; raw current includes differently charged shared file caches and kernel memory.
Observed approximately 84 MiB drops track worker retirement; schedules interrupt the 300-second windows, so no uninterrupted five-minute or multiday-idle guarantee is established.
Recovery received logs alone do not establish completed recovery. Four repeat runs independently passed injected retry/recovery/completion/stale-result checks after memory sampling.
Peak lower bounds use one-second simultaneous samples; upper bounds sum independent per-service lifetime peaks.
Two initial runs predate runtime fault checks and metadata-language result recording; feature request sequence is otherwise comparable.
PSS sums across distinct service cgroups can include proportional shared mappings that differ from cgroup file ownership.

Worker retirement log offsets are estimated from final PSS file modification time and one-second sampling; allow approximately two seconds uncertainty. Baseline2 retires a worker at the start of the final window; the later 130-second cgroup drop is not its first retirement.
